stops.note: 'an addition, increase', related to the verb ēcan 'to add', which survives in 'to eke out'
'an additional name'; the Promptorium Parvulorum, the first English-Latin dictionary (c. 1440), lists both 'neke name, or eke name', as 'an ekename' was being heard as 'a nekename'
the n stolen from the article stuck, and the vowel shifted to 'nick'

current_meaning: a familiar or humorous name used instead of a real name
